## Introduction
For Lab 7, I constructed a hardware accelerator to perform 128-bit AES encryption. I set up a SPI interface to send a plaintext message and key from my MCU to the accelerator and verify that the cyphertext received back is correct. 

## Technical Documentation
The source code for the project can be found in the associated [Github repository](https://github.com/isabella-vera/E155/tree/main/Lab7)

## AI Prototype Summary
I completed the AI prototype using Gemini and the two given prompts.

Here is the code I got when I uploaded the file:
```
module aes_key_expansion (
    input  logic [127:0] prev_key,   // Previous key / initial key [w0, w1, w2, w3]
    input  logic [3:0]   rcon_idx,   // Round constant index (1 to 10 for AES-128)
    output logic [127:0] next_key    // Calculated round key [w4, w5, w6, w7]
);

    // Break the input key into 4 32-bit words
    logic [31:0] w0, w1, w2, w3;
    assign {w0, w1, w2, w3} = prev_key;

    // Temporary variables for word operations
    logic [31:0] rot_w3;
    logic [31:0] sub_w3;
    logic [31:0] rcon_w;
    logic [31:0] temp;

    // Output key words
    logic [31:0] w4, w5, w6, w7;

    // Function to calculate Rcon[j] byte based on round index (Section 5.2 / Table 5)
    function automatic logic [7:0] get_rcon(input logic [3:0] idx);
        case (idx)
            4'd1:  get_rcon = 8'h01;
            4'd2:  get_rcon = 8'h02;
            4'd3:  get_rcon = 8'h04;
            4'd4:  get_rcon = 8'h08;
            4'd5:  get_rcon = 8'h10;
            4'd6:  get_rcon = 8'h20;
            4'd7:  get_rcon = 8'h40;
            4'd8:  get_rcon = 8'h80;
            4 me9:  get_rcon = 8'h1B;
            4'd10: get_rcon = 8'h36;
            default: get_rcon = 8'h00;
        endcase
    endfunction

    // Instantiate existing RotWord module: RotWord([a0, a1, a2, a3]) = [a1, a2, a3, a0]
    RotWord rot_inst (
        .in  (w3),
        .out (rot_w3)
    );

    // Instantiate existing SubWord module: Applies S-box to each of the 4 bytes
    SubWord sub_inst (
        .in  (rot_w3),
        .out (sub_w3)
    );

    // Rcon word is formed as [Rcon[i/Nk], 00, 00, 00]
    assign rcon_w = {get_rcon(rcon_idx), 24'h000000};

    // temp = SubWord(RotWord(w[i-1])) ^ Rcon[i/Nk]
    assign temp = sub_w3 ^ rcon_w;

    // Calculate the 4 output key words recursively
    assign w4 = w0 ^ temp;
    assign w5 = w1 ^ w4;
    assign w6 = w2 ^ w5;
    assign w7 = w3 ^ w6;

    // Output the newly expanded 128-bit key
    assign next_key = {w4, w5, w6, w7};

endmodule

```

Without the upload, I got this:
```
module key_expansion #(
    parameter int Nk = 4,  // Number of 32-bit words in the key (e.g., 4, 6, 8)
    parameter int Nr = 10  // Number of rounds (e.g., 10, 12, 14)
)(
    input  logic [32*Nk-1:0]      key,
    input  logic [31:0]           Rcon [0:4*Nr+3], // Rcon array indexed by word
    output logic [31:0]           w    [0:4*Nr+3]
);

    // Dynamic length based on Nr: Total words needed = 4 * Nr + 4
    localparam int TOTAL_WORDS = 4 * Nr + 4;

    // Temporary signals for module outputs and processed temp values
    logic [31:0] mod2_out [Nk:TOTAL_WORDS-1];
    logic [31:0] mod1_out [Nk:TOTAL_WORDS-1];
    logic [31:0] temp     [Nk:TOTAL_WORDS-1];

    // =========================================================================
    // 1. Initial key loading (i = 0 to Nk - 1)
    // =========================================================================
    genvar i;
    generate
        for (i = 0; i < Nk; i++) begin : gen_initial_key
            // Slice key from key[4*i .. 4*i+3] (4 bytes = 32 bits per word)
            // Big-endian index ordering: key[4*i +: 4]
            assign w[i] = {key[8*(4*i+3) +: 8], 
                           key[8*(4*i+2) +: 8], 
                           key[8*(4*i+1) +: 8], 
                           key[8*(4*i)   +: 8]};
        end
    endgenerate

    // =========================================================================
    // 2. Main key expansion loop (i = Nk to 4*Nr + 3)
    // =========================================================================
    generate
        for (i = Nk; i < TOTAL_WORDS; i++) begin : gen_key_expansion

            // -----------------------------------------------------------------
            // Condition 1: i mod Nk == 0
            // -----------------------------------------------------------------
            if (i % Nk == 0) begin : cond_mod_nk_zero
                module2 u_module2 (
                    .in  (w[i-1]),
                    .out (mod2_out[i])
                );

                module1 u_module1 (
                    .in  (mod2_out[i]),
                    .out (mod1_out[i])
                );

                // temp = module1(module2(w[i-1])) ^ Rcon[i/Nk]
                assign temp[i] = mod1_out[i] ^ Rcon[i / Nk];
            end

            // -----------------------------------------------------------------
            // Condition 2: Nk > 6 and i mod Nk == 4
            // -----------------------------------------------------------------
            else if ((Nk > 6) && (i % Nk == 4)) begin : cond_mod_nk_four
                module1 u_module1 (
                    .in  (w[i-1]),
                    .out (mod1_out[i])
                );

                // temp = module1(w[i-1])
                assign temp[i] = mod1_out[i];
            end

            // -----------------------------------------------------------------
            // Default Condition: Neither of the above
            // -----------------------------------------------------------------
            else begin : cond_default
                // temp = w[i-1]
                assign temp[i] = w[i-1];
            end

            // -----------------------------------------------------------------
            // Word output calculation: w[i] = w[i-Nk] ^ temp
            // -----------------------------------------------------------------
            assign w[i] = w[i-Nk] ^ temp[i];

        end
    endgenerate

endmodule
```

I was surprised that even when I said not to use any knowledge of the AES standard, the second output still recognized the keyexpansion logic and called the module key_expansion.
